title: Romance Advice I Wish My Parents Taught Me: the Medium windows

items.title: “Then what? You block her?”
items.where: Can Casual Sex or a Situationship Actually Be Honest?, P3
items.my_version: That’s honest about what you want tonight, but don't forget that tonight is enough time to make a baby. If this girl gets pregnant, she’s gonna call you, and then what? You block her, or you agree to child support? Try to convince her to abort if she thinks abortion is killing her child? My first girlfriend, a diehard Baptist, aborted our child and told me a year later, because she “didn’t want to trap” me. I'm still shocked and saddened about that, 20 years later (assuming it was true). This is what penetrative sex can do. No contraception is perfect.

items.title: Sex appeal “isn’t the basis anymore”
items.where: And deeper is the point, P1
items.my_version: Beyond all that practical stuff, sex is extremely important for building and renewing the connection. I also think that if two people aren’t having sex, it becomes hard to explain how they’re different from regular friends. But if the connection gets deep enough, sex appeal isn’t the basis of the relationship anymore. You don’t stop loving the person because she got old, he lost his job, one of you got sick, or sex became impossible.

items.title: “How well we actually handle our own issues”
items.my_version: I’d want both of us to be honest about how well we actually handle our own issues. What addictions or impulsive behaviors can’t we reliably control? What are we probably going to ask forgiveness for more than once? That tells me more than either of us proclaiming that we’re healed.

items.title: “Because if somebody starts with enough trauma”
items.my_version: We see what we want to see. Their meditations may have helped them a lot, but I still had no idea how either woman would act when a relationship got ugly, because if somebody starts with enough trauma, huge progress can still leave a lot unresolved.

items.title: Twin flames, and the women you still love
items.where: Beware idealization in either direction, P7
items.my_version:
I’ve learned to get nervous when somebody "knows" too much about me/us too soon. You know how it goes: “We’re twin flames!” or “I’m Lord Krishna and she’s Radha!” Okay, maybe I really am way better than the other guys she’s found. But if she hasn’t found anything about me that bothers her yet, she hasn’t found all of me.

For example, I still love women I’ve loved before, and sometimes I talk about them, with no intention of making my current partner jealous, just because I’m thinking about them and I don’t want to hide it. If she can’t handle the truth that I still love them, she isn’t ready for me.

items.title: “Much stronger barriers than these”
items.where: If slow isn’t realistic for you, P3
items.my_version: Phone or video first can help, as can meeting up around other people and deciding beforehand that we aren’t going home together. Islamic and conservative Christian cultures put much stronger barriers than these around a man and woman being alone before marriage. I don’t accept their helicoptering solution, but they noticed something real. We don’t live in tribes anymore, where people around us might know both of us well enough to slow this down.

items.title: “But woops, I came too fast”
items.my_version: I find the intuitive mind incredibly sexy, because I can’t fully follow it. During sex, some of the most “womanly” women I’ve loved have gone through psychic experiences, memories that felt like past lives, and things I had no idea how to explain. One time, Bee said she almost got enlightened, but woops, I came too fast.

items.title: “With H., I learned”
items.where: Two Pillars Don’t Hold The Roof Up, P9
items.my_version: With H., I learned another part of the same dyad problem: not to treat what either of us thought the relationship was as a guarantee of what it would remain, because feelings can and usually do change over time. In our case, the relationship continued to naturally deepen while our outside relationships often felt more shallow, so it was natural for the dependency to increase. She was never into monogamy, but that didn’t stop her from becoming possessive once she found someone really worth keeping. And then she began demonizing me when I refused to be possessed. Because we did not have a shared community capable of supporting us, her friends heard her side and affirmed her truth.

items.title: “That drove me crazy, because”
items.where: If you’re already in it, P4
items.my_version: Even dishonesty was sometimes hard for me to define in these relationships. Bee once opened a door and, a second later, said she hadn’t opened it. That drove me crazy, because why would she lie like that? On the other hand, although she was technically lying, there was no strategy behind it, and she was usually quite honest. Non-strategic lying is literally defined as "pathological lying," so I should have seen it more like an illness than a failure of virtue.

items.title: What does “without manipulating ... all that expert management” mean?
items.where: From flow to nitty gritty, P2
items.question: In the last sentence of “From flow to nitty gritty”, what is the “expert management”, and who would be manipulating whom? It said “without manipulating based on all that expert “management,”” and a fresh reader found that clause can’t be parsed; the sentence is the section’s last Medium window. My guess: she expects me to read her mind and check in all the time, and to manage her feelings like an expert without it turning into manipulation. If that’s it, I’ll write it that way and test it.

items.title: What’s off in these three places?
items.where: Two Pillars Don’t Hold The Roof Up, P2
items.question: The first part of “Two Pillars Don’t Hold The Roof Up” reads Medium in three places (highlighted), and all three of my tries read worse. A reader could stumble on three things: “That’s a pretty terrible time to be trying to run the rest of life with two people” runs the falling-out into the point that two people alone have no backup; “Separate confidants can be helpful and harmful” is a line the next two sentences say again; and “take what they say with a grain of salt” says again what the sentence before says (they’re biased toward you). Is it one of these, or something else?
